question: Should rich countries pay billions to build leading-edge chip factories at home?
answer: Nearly all of the most advanced logic chips come from Taiwan, across a strait from China, which claims the island. A blockade would halt cars, phones and weapons worldwide at once. The US CHIPS Act of 2022 set aside $39 billion in factory grants: insurance, and cheap against a shock that size.
move: Whichever side you took, ask whether a factory ends a dependence or just moves it.
ask: When I want independence from someone, am I ending the dependence or just moving it elsewhere?
counterpoint: Chipmaking runs on a web no nation owns: Dutch lithography, Japanese chemicals, American design software, Taiwanese know-how. A fab in Arizona still needs all of them, and TSMC delayed its first plant there, citing a shortage of skilled workers. Subsidies may buy factories that open a generation behind, while the real dependence stays where it was.
reference: CHIPS and Science Act, Public Law 117-167, US Congress, 2022
